To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the levels of AHA1 and stomatin-like protein-2 (SLP2) proteins were found to be significantly increased in OS as compared to osteoblastic cells by 2-D gel proteomic analysis.
AHA1 and stomatin-like protein are significantly over-produced in OS cells as comapred to normal osteoblasts, which suggests they may be effective biomarkers for the identification of osteosarcoma.
AHA1 and SL2P are significantly increased in the OS cells, as compared to the osteoblastic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that are differentially expressed in OS and osteoarthritis cells.
the identification of biomarkers to distinguish OS from normal osteoblast cells.
the discovery of new biomarkers for the early detection of OS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study identified AHA1 and SL2P as potential OS cell markers.
the present study has provided a useful approach to identifying candidate biomarkers to differentiate OS cells from normal osteogenic cells.
the proteomic approach can be a powerful tool for the identification of candidate biomarkers for the diagnosis of OS cells.

we have identified several proteins that were differentially expressed in OS and normal osteoblastic (osteogenic) cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of immortalized normal cells as controls in proteomic studies is critical for identifying biomarkers of tumor cells.
